newsitem.title: CHILE: Chilean shares end higher in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: Chilean shares end higher in thin trade.

text.p: Chilean stocks ended firmer in quiet pre-holiday trading, with an afternoon technical rally petering out by the close, brokers said.
The blue-chip IPSA index ended 1.02 percent higher at 114.54 points. The general IGPA index ended 0.6 percent higher at 5293.94 points on modest volume of 14.8 billion pesos.

Trading was quiet, with every other major Latin American bourse closed until Monday and little local news to move the market, brokers said. Technical buying gave the market a boost in the afternoon, sending the IPSA up about 1.5 percent, but profit takers then moved in, they said.
The rise brought the IPSA's gains so far this year to 14.5 percent, a strong recovery after 1996, but still short of the bullish trend many analysts have been expecting this year.
Gainers included Enersis, up 1.2 percent to 255 points before its shareholders' meeting set for Wednesday, and Telex-Chile, up 4.9 percent to 1,050 points.
Endesa, which has its own shareholders' meeting Tuesday, ended 0.6 percent higher to 254.50 points.
Decliners included Campos, off 1.1 to 87 pesos, and Banco Edwards, which slipped one percent to 50.5 pesos.
